title: The Banach–Tarski Paradox
beats: Chocolate-bar vanishing trick: cuts and rearrangement appear to create a square
Debunks it as an illusion: every piece is slightly shorter; animation hides the cheat
Real theorem: one object into 5 pieces, rearranged into two exact copies
Says we must first ask what infinity is before the proof
Infinity is a size, not a number; countable vs uncountable defined
Tries to count reals from 0 and gets stuck: where do you even start
Cantor diagonal: change digit n of number n to build a number missing from the list
Evens equal all whole numbers by pairing; infinity over 2 is infinity
Hilbert's hotel: shift guests to add or remove one; infinity plus or minus one
Hotel applied to a circle: remove one point, shift countable irrational-step points to fill it
Hyperwebster dictionary: dropping the initial a from the A volume gives the whole dictionary
Poses the plan: turn the sphere into a Hyperwebster and name points by rotation sequences
Four rotations, finite words, no backtracking, written right to left
Worked examples of four strings, colour-coded by last rotation
Cover the uncountably many points by choosing new starting points; poles coloured yellow as exceptions
Cut sphere into colour pieces; the left piece rotated right becomes L, U, D and starting points: quarter becomes three quarters
Make second copy using up piece, fix starting points with strings of Us, patch poles and centre with the circle trick
One sphere into two without adding anything: 1 plus 1 equals 1
Real-world: pieces are infinitely complex, so impossible physically; possible link to particle collisions
Closing philosophy: common sense is limited, the universe is not strange, we are
Book recommendations, Field Day plug, sign-off

new_moves.name: debunk-the-fake-version
new_moves.what: Open with a fake instance of the paradox, expose its cheat, then reveal the real theorem

new_moves.name: stepping-stone-trick-chain
new_moves.what: Teach one trick (shift to absorb a missing element) in four increasingly geometric settings before the final proof

new_moves.name: hide-the-proof-behind-a-roadmap-sentence
new_moves.what: Declares the proof will reuse the earlier trick so learner can follow

theory: The video teaches by installing one portable trick (an infinite set can absorb a shift to hide a hole) across escalating settings, so the final 8-minute proof is a recognisable recombination rather than new machinery. The fake-chocolate opener sets the learner's suspicion that the trick must be cheating, which makes the later honest caveat feel earned.
velocity: Orchestrator: sequence stepping stones so one reusable mechanism is shown 3+ times before the real problem
Scene builder: colour-coded set pieces with 'rotate piece, reduce backtracks' animations; keep notation to four letters
Learner model: do not start notation until concept stated; track whether learner failed to count reals before diagonal
Voice: an honest caveat at the end about physical impossibility; budget a late-caveat beat
Evals: check that a fake-then-real hook has the debunk explicit
quote: The universe isn't strange. We are.
